Resolves #19887

README's maintainer table now links Euclid, Julia and Mnemosyne by their current logins, and so do its roster sentence and three blog posts. The renames freed `neo-gpt`, `neo-gemini-pro` and `neo-fable`. GitHub keeps no redirect for a renamed user, so the old links return 404 and anyone can register those names. neomjs.com builds from the npm package, so these files have to be right on `dev` before the 13.3.0 cut. #19784 fixes the release notes' logins, and its README line 150 does not touch these hunks.

Evidence: L1 (static: `git grep` and `gh api users/<login>` on the head). Docs only, no runtime path. Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `git grep -nE 'github\.com/(neo-gpt\|neo-gemini-pro\|neo-fable)([)"/#?]\|$)'` on d68e88c1f6 matches only `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v13.3.0.md:19`, which #19784 rewrites. |
| AC-2 | All 14 single-segment `github.com/<login>` links in the maintainer table resolve via `gh api users/<login>`. `neo-gpt`, `neo-gemini-pro` and `neo-fable` return 404. |
| AC-3 | `git show --numstat`: README.md 4/4, the three posts 1/1, 2/2, 1/1. Every changed line only swaps a login. |

## Deltas from ticket

- None. The cross-family post keeps its link text "Neo Gemini Pro", the account's name when the post was written. Only the URL changes.

## Test Evidence

- Pre-commit: secrets, whitespace and relative-link checks passed.
- Same accounts: `gh pr view` reports #19688, #19740 and #19809 as authored by `neo-gpt-euclid`, `neo-gemini-julia` and `neo-fable-mnemosyne`.

## Post-Merge Validation

- None. The published pages pick these files up with the 13.3.0 package (#19652).
